title: Euro banknotes and coins enter circulation
text: On 1 January 2002 euro banknotes and coins were introduced in twelve countries, replacing national currencies such as the Deutsche Mark, the French franc and the Italian lira. It was the largest cash changeover in history.

title: Speech by Mario Draghi at the Global Investment Conference, London
text: During the euro area sovereign debt crisis, President Mario Draghi told investors in London that, within its mandate, the ECB was ready to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro, and that this would be enough. Bond spreads of vulnerable countries fell sharply in the following months.

title: ECB assumes responsibility for banking supervision
text: On 4 November 2014 the ECB took over the supervision of the largest banks in the euro area under the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM), working together with national supervisors. Smaller banks remain supervised by national authorities.

title: Christine Lagarde takes office as ECB President
text: Christine Lagarde took office as President of the European Central Bank on 1 November 2019 for a non-renewable term of eight years, succeeding Mario Draghi.

title: ECB concludes its strategy review
text: The Governing Council adopted a symmetric inflation target of 2% over the medium term: negative and positive deviations from the target are equally undesirable. The ECB also agreed an action plan to include climate change considerations in its monetary policy framework and recommended including owner-occupied housing costs in the inflation measure over time.

title: Monetary policy decisions, December 2021
text: The Governing Council decided to discontinue net asset purchases under the pandemic emergency purchase programme (PEPP) at the end of March 2022. Principal payments from maturing PEPP securities will be reinvested until at least the end of 2024.

title: Monetary policy decisions, June 2022
text: The Governing Council decided to end net asset purchases under its asset purchase programme (APP) as of 1 July 2022. It intends to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points at its July meeting, and expects to raise them again in September.

title: Monetary policy decisions, July 2022
text: The Governing Council decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 50 basis points, the first increase in eleven years. The deposit facility rate rises to 0.00%, the main refinancing operations rate to 0.50% and the marginal lending facility rate to 0.75%.

title: The Transmission Protection Instrument
text: The Governing Council approved the Transmission Protection Instrument (TPI) to counter unwarranted, disorderly market dynamics that pose a serious threat to the transmission of monetary policy across the euro area. Under the TPI, the Eurosystem can buy securities of jurisdictions experiencing a deterioration in financing conditions not warranted by country-specific fundamentals.

title: Monetary policy decisions, September 2022
text: The Governing Council decided to raise the three key ECB interest rates by 75 basis points. The deposit facility rate rises to 0.75% and the main refinancing operations rate to 1.25%.

title: Monetary policy decisions, October 2022
text: The Governing Council raised the three key ECB interest rates by 75 basis points, bringing the deposit facility rate to 1.50%. It also changed the terms and conditions of the third series of targeted longer-term refinancing operations (TLTRO III) to support the normalisation of bank funding costs.

title: Economic Bulletin: inflation developments
text: Euro area annual inflation, measured by the Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP), peaked at 10.6% in October 2022, driven by soaring energy and food prices after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

title: Monetary policy decisions, December 2022
text: The Governing Council raised the key ECB interest rates by 50 basis points, the deposit facility rate reaching 2.00%. From the beginning of March 2023 the APP portfolio will decline by 15 billion euro per month on average, as not all principal payments from maturing securities will be reinvested.

title: Croatia joins the euro area
text: On 1 January 2023 Croatia adopted the euro, becoming the 20th member of the euro area. Hrvatska narodna banka joined the Eurosystem.

title: Monetary policy decisions, February 2023
text: The Governing Council raised the three key ECB interest rates by 50 basis points; the deposit facility rate rises to 2.50%.

title: Monetary policy decisions, March 2023
text: The Governing Council raised the three key ECB interest rates by 50 basis points, bringing the deposit facility rate to 3.00%, while monitoring tensions in financial markets.

title: Monetary policy decisions, May 2023
text: The Governing Council raised the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points, the deposit facility rate reaching 3.25%. It expects to discontinue reinvestments under the APP as of July 2023.

title: Monetary policy decisions, June 2023
text: The Governing Council raised the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points; the deposit facility rate rises to 3.50%.

title: Monetary policy decisions, July 2023
text: The Governing Council raised the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points; the deposit facility rate rises to 3.75%.

title: Monetary policy decisions, September 2023
text: The Governing Council raised the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points, the tenth consecutive increase. The deposit facility rate reaches 4.00%, the main refinancing operations rate 4.50% and the marginal lending facility rate 4.75%.

title: Digital euro: preparation phase
text: The Governing Council decided to move to the preparation phase of the digital euro project, starting on 1 November 2023 and lasting two years, to lay the foundations for a possible issuance of a digital euro.

title: Changes to the operational framework
text: The Governing Council will keep steering the monetary policy stance through the deposit facility rate. As of 18 September 2024, the spread between the main refinancing operations rate and the deposit facility rate will be reduced to 15 basis points.

title: Monetary policy decisions, June 2024
text: The Governing Council decided to lower the three key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points, its first cut since 2019, after nine months of holding rates steady. The deposit facility rate falls to 3.75%.

title: Monetary policy decisions, September 2024
text: The Governing Council decided to lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 3.50%. With the new operational framework, the main refinancing operations rate falls to 3.65%.

title: Monetary policy decisions, October 2024
text: The Governing Council decided to lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 3.25%, as the disinflationary process is well on track.

title: Monetary policy decisions, December 2024
text: The Governing Council decided to lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 3.00%. Reinvestments under the PEPP ended at the end of 2024.

title: Monetary policy decisions, January 2025
text: The Governing Council decided to lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 2.75%.

title: Monetary policy decisions, March 2025
text: The Governing Council decided to lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 2.50%.

title: Monetary policy decisions, April 2025
text: The Governing Council decided to lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 2.25%, citing the uncertain outlook created by trade tensions.

title: Monetary policy decisions, June 2025
text: The Governing Council decided to lower the deposit facility rate by 25 basis points to 2.00%, with inflation close to the 2% medium-term target.

title: Bulgaria to join the euro area
text: The Council of the European Union approved Bulgaria's adoption of the euro on 1 January 2026, making it the 21st member of the euro area.
